Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details:
The failing test `testOptionGroupLong` demonstrates that when an option with only a long name (no short name) is added to an OptionGroup, selecting that option by its long name during parsing does not properly mark it as selected in the group.

Examining the `OptionGroup.setSelected(Option)` method reveals the core issue:
- The method checks if `selected` is null or if `selected.equals(option.getOpt())`.
- It then sets `selected` to `option.getOpt()`.
- If another option is already selected and is different, it throws an exception.

The `Option.getOpt()` method returns the short option name, which may be null if the option was created with only a long option name and no short option.

In the test, options are created only with long option names (`foo` and `bar`) and no short option. Consequently, `option.getOpt()` returns null. Therefore, when `OptionGroup.setSelected(option)` uses `option.getOpt()`, it gets null and this makes `selected` null or fails to set the selected option key properly.

The `OptionGroup` stores options in a map keyed by `option.getKey()`. Looking at `Option.getKey()`, it returns `longOpt` if `opt` is null, which is the correct key to find options without short names.

Hence, the mismatch between `setSelected` using `option.getOpt()` (which could return null) versus the storage key being `option.getKey()` (which correctly uses long option if short is missing) makes the selection mechanism fail when options lack short names.

This matches the current bug report description: "If the selected option hasn't a short name, group.setSelected(option) has no effect." The root cause is that `OptionGroup.setSelected` uses `option.getOpt()` instead of `option.getKey()` to set the selected option.

This issue explains why the test fails: the selected option is not tracked properly in the group when only a long option is used.

The recent bug reports are unrelated, discussing other issues with OptionBuilder and parser unification.

In conclusion, the bug arises because `OptionGroup.setSelected(Option)` uses the option's short name (`getOpt()`) rather than the appropriate key (`getKey()`) that supports long-only options for selecting options in groups.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
